newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Kabila meets Zimbabwe's Mugabe, keeps war option.
newsitem.headline: Kabila meets Zimbabwe's Mugabe, keeps war option.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila met Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe over peace efforts to end the civil war in Zaire on Thursday, Zimbabwe's state news agency ZIANA said.
Kabila was quoted by ZIANA as saying that he retained the option of war to conquer President Mobutu Sese Seko.
The rebel leader flew into Harare unannounced for a meeting with Mugabe, who assumes the chair of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) next month.
Asked whether his forces -- which have captured more than half of Zaire in a seven-month military campaign against Mobutu -- would continue fighting in the face of pending peace talks, Kabila said:
"Why not? I think we must go forward. We must liberate Kinshasa but we are now discussing with others to try and solve the problem by peaceful means."

Kabila said the talks on a South African ship in international waters off Central Africa would take place on Saturday. "I have been told it will now be on Saturday because Mobutu has changed his mind again."

There has been some confusion on the date of the first face-to-face meeting between Mobutu and Kabila with South Africa saying it would take place on Friday, Mobutu's spokesman saying on Saturday and Kabila's aides on Sunday.
ZIANA said Kabila flew into Harare from the Zairean southern town of Lumumbashi to brief and seek Mugabe's political support.
The agency quoted Mugabe as saying he hoped Kabila and Mobutu would agree at the planned peace talks "on the way forward for the sake of peace and stability in the region".
"My own attitude is to wish them well and hope this meeting will produce some understanding that will lead the people of Zaire to new peace," Mugabe said.
